questions.question_text: To convert a capacity from L to kL, what must you do?

options.why: Reversed the direction; a kilolitre is larger than a litre, so the count of units goes down.
Used a factor of $100$, but every step on the capacity ladder is a factor of $1000$.
Applied two ladder steps, landing at megalitres instead of kilolitres.

questions.solution_text:
A kilolitre is larger than a litre, so the count of units goes down and the conversion divides.
Every step on the capacity ladder is a factor of $1000$.
Divide by $1000$.

questions.question_text: Which is the larger amount, $2500\text{ cm}^3$ or $2.4$ L? Give the larger amount in millilitres.

options.why: Read $2500\text{ cm}^3$ as $2.5$ mL by dividing by $1000$, then chose the other amount.
Multiplied $2500\text{ cm}^3$ by $1000$ instead of using $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1$ mL.
Multiplied $2.4$ L by $1\,000\,000$, using a cubic-metre factor instead of $1000$.

questions.solution_text:
$2500\text{ cm}^3$
$= 2500\text{ mL}$
$2.4\text{ L} \times 1000$
$= 2400\text{ mL}$
$2500 > 2400$, so the amount given in cubic centimetres is larger.
$2500\text{ mL}$

questions.question_text: A student converts a volume from $\text{m}^3$ to $\text{cm}^3$ by multiplying by $100$, because there are $100$ cm in a metre. What should the student multiply by?

options.why: Kept the length factor, ignoring that a cubic metre is $100$ cm along each of three edges.
Squared the length factor $100$, which is the area factor, not the volume factor.
Used the factor that links cubic centimetres and cubic millimetres instead of $100^3$.

questions.solution_text:
A cubic metre is $100$ cm along each of three edges.
$100 \times 100 \times 100 = 1\,000\,000$
The student should multiply by $1\,000\,000$.
